components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
矢 (arrow) with a flag 方: a clan or troop gathered under its banner, with arrows at hand.

example.hanzi: 这个家族已经在这座城市生活了几百年。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiāzú yǐjīng zài zhè zuò chéngshì shēnghuó le jǐ bǎi nián.
example.english: This family has lived in this city for hundreds of years.
example.fact: 家族 refers to an extended clan or lineage spanning generations, distinct from 家庭 (“family” in the narrower sense of one household — parents and children) — conflating the two is a common learner slip, since English “family” covers both senses with a single word.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì yí ge dà jiāzú.
examples.english: We are a big family.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jiāzú de gùshi hěn cháng.
examples.english: This family's story is very long.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 慢 is a slow, unhurried heart.
曼 (màn) sounds exactly like 慢; also in 漫 màn.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 慢 is a slow, unhurried heart.
曼 (màn) sounds exactly like 慢; also in 漫 màn.

example.hanzi: 请慢慢说,我听不太懂。
example.pinyin: Qǐng mànmàn shuō, wǒ tīng bú tài dǒng.
example.english: Please speak slowly, I don't quite understand.
example.fact: Reduplicating a one-syllable adjective like 慢 into 慢慢 is one of Mandarin's most productive ways to turn a description into a gentle adverb of manner — in fast, casual speech the second syllable often gets a light neutral-toned “mān” rather than the full fourth tone, even though dictionaries still print it as màn.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ mànmàn chī, bié zháojí.
examples.english: Eat slowly, no rush.

examples.pinyin: Tiānqì mànmàn biàn lěng le.
examples.english: The weather is gradually getting cold.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person bowing low; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
氐 (dī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 底 dǐ and 抵 dǐ.

example.hanzi: 请把声音放低一点。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shēngyīn fàng dī yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please keep your voice down a little.
example.fact: 低 is the opposite of 高 and also a verb: 低头 (lower the head, or yield). 低声 is a low voice, 低价 low price, 低碳 low-carbon, and 低头族 is slang for "heads-down" phone addicts.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi tài dī le.
examples.english: This table is too low.

examples.hanzi: 他低着头走路，没看见我。
examples.pinyin: Tā dī zhe tóu zǒulù, méi kànjiàn wǒ.
examples.english: He walked with his head down and didn't see me.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting and blades: 利, 别, 到; 剩 is what remains after cutting.
乘 (chéng) is close to shèng; also in 盛 shèng.

example.hanzi: 盘子里还剩一块蛋糕。
example.pinyin: Pánzi lǐ hái shèng yí kuài dàngāo.
example.english: There is one slice of cake left on the plate.
example.fact: 剩 is to be left over: 剩下 (be left), 剩饭 (leftover rice), 剩菜 (leftovers). 剩女 ("leftover women") is a contested term for unmarried women past their late twenties, often considered derogatory.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǐ shèng wǔ fēnzhōng le.
examples.english: We only have five minutes left.

examples.pinyin: Chīwán fàn, hái shèng hěn duō cài.
examples.english: After the meal, there's a lot of food left.

components.note: 戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
斗 (dipper) — a measuring dipper with a handle; as a radical it marks measuring: 料, 科, 斜. Also read dǒu (a measure) or dòu (to fight).

example.hanzi: 士兵们在战斗中表现得非常勇敢。
example.pinyin: Shìbīng men zài zhàndòu zhōng biǎoxiàn de fēicháng yǒnggǎn.
example.english: The soldiers showed great courage in the battle.
example.fact: 战斗 sits at the serious, organized-combat end of Mandarin's “fight” vocabulary — a schoolyard scuffle or a shouting match instead reaches for 打架 or 吵架, reserving 战斗 for war, military combat, or a figuratively hard-fought struggle.

examples.hanzi: 他们在战斗中非常勇敢。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài zhàndòu zhōng fēicháng yǒnggǎn.
examples.english: They were very brave in the battle.

examples.hanzi: 游戏里的角色可以战斗。
examples.pinyin: Yóuxì lǐ de juésè kěyǐ zhàndòu.
examples.english: The characters in the game can fight.

components.note: 饣 (food, simplified 食) — meals and eating: 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling; 饭 is cooked rice or a meal.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match for fàn; also in 板 bǎn.

example.hanzi: 我们去吃饭吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù chīfàn ba.
example.english: Let's go eat.
example.fact: 饭 is both cooked rice and a meal: 米饭 (rice), 早饭 (breakfast), 吃饭 (eat a meal). 吃饭了吗？ ("Have you eaten?") is a common greeting in China. 饭店 means restaurant or hotel.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi chīfàn, dùzi hěn è.
examples.english: I haven't eaten yet and I'm very hungry.

examples.hanzi: 今天的晚饭是米饭和鱼。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de wǎnfàn shì mǐfàn hé yú.
examples.english: Today's dinner is rice and fish.

components.note: 复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.
木 (tree) — the bottom part, as in 林 forest and 树 tree; in old 雜 the tree or clothing bits show collecting many things. Treat as a loose hint only.
九 (nine) — the top part; 杂 is simplified from 雜. Memory aid: nine kinds of wood piled up, a mix.

example.hanzi: 这道数学题太复杂了,我做不出来。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào shùxué tí tài fùzá le, wǒ zuò bu chūlái.
example.english: This math problem is too complicated, I can't solve it.
example.fact: 复 alone already carries a sense of “repeating, compounding” (as in 复习, “to review”), so 复杂 literally suggests something with many layers stacked on top of each other — its clean opposite, 简单 (“simple”), is one of the first antonym pairs Mandarin learners memorize.

examples.hanzi: 这件事比你想的更复杂。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì bǐ nǐ xiǎng de gèng fùzá.
examples.english: This matter is more complicated than you think.

examples.hanzi: 地铁线路太复杂了，我总是迷路。
examples.pinyin: Dìtiě xiànlù tài fùzá le, wǒ zǒngshì mílù.
examples.english: The subway lines are too complicated, and I always get lost.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 肚 belly, 脚 foot, 脸 face, 胖 fat; 脑 is the brain.
The right half shows hair over a skull and also sounds out 恼 nǎo and 瑙 nǎo.

example.hanzi: 他很聪明，脑子转得快。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn cōngming, nǎozi zhuàn de kuài.
example.english: He's clever and thinks quickly.
example.fact: 脑 is the brain: 脑子 (brain, mind), 大脑 (cerebrum), 头脑 (mind) and 脑袋 (head, colloquial). 电脑 ("electric brain") is the everyday word for a computer.

examples.pinyin: Tā de nǎozi lǐ quán shì gōngzuò.
examples.english: His mind is full of work.

examples.hanzi: 我头脑发昏，什么都想不起来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóunǎo fā hūn, shénme dōu xiǎng bu qǐlái.
examples.english: I feel dizzy and can't remember anything.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福; 社 was an altar to the earth god 土.
土 (earth) — the earth god worshipped at the altar; hence a community that gathers there: society.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 教育对社会的发展非常重要。
example.pinyin: Jiàoyù duì shèhuì de fāzhǎn fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.english: Education is very important for the development of society.
example.fact: 社 originally named the local earth-god shrine that a village community gathered around to worship — 社会's modern sense of “society” grew directly out of that older image of a community bound together by a shared gathering place.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个有很多问题的社会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge yǒu hěn duō wèntí de shèhuì.
examples.english: This is a society with many problems.

examples.hanzi: 毕业后他走进社会，开始工作。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè hòu tā zǒujìn shèhuì, kāishǐ gōngzuò.
examples.english: After graduating he stepped into society and started working.

components.note: 火 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 灯 lamp, 烧 burn, 热 hot: a hot, fevered head, hence vexed.
页 (head) is a loose sound clue for fán; as a meaning part 页 means head or page.

example.hanzi: 我今天心里很烦。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān xīnlǐ hěn fán.
example.english: I'm feeling annoyed today.
example.fact: 烦 is annoyed or annoying: 烦人 (irritating), 烦恼 (worries), 麻烦 (trouble). 麻烦你 + verb ("sorry to trouble you to…") is a very polite way to ask a favour: 麻烦你帮我拿一下.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì zhēn fánrén.
examples.english: This matter is really annoying.

examples.pinyin: Bié fán wǒ, wǒ zhèng mángzhe ne.
examples.english: Don't bother me; I'm busy.

components.note: 古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue for gù; 古 also in 姑 gū and 固 gù.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: an action with a cause.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 我不是故意的,真的很抱歉。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì gùyì de, zhēn de hěn bàoqiàn.
example.english: I didn't do it on purpose, I'm really sorry.
example.fact: “不是故意的” (“I didn't mean to”) is one of the most common apologies in spoken Mandarin, with 故意 as its key word — its natural comeback, 不小心 (“carelessly, accidentally”), is worth learning alongside it as the paired excuse.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì gùyì chídào de ma?
examples.english: Did he arrive late on purpose?

examples.pinyin: Tā gùyì bǎ mén guānshàng le.
examples.english: She closed the door deliberately.

components.note: 阝 (city, right-side form of 邑) — towns and places: 都, 部, 那, 邮; 邻 is people in the same neighborhood.
令 (lìng) is only a loose stand-in for the sound lín.
尸 (a sitting person, body) — a figure at rest or a building: 屋 house, 层 floor, 尾 tail; 居 is to dwell.
古 (gǔ) is a loose clue; 居 jū sounds out 据 jù, 剧 jù and 锯 jù.

example.hanzi: 我们的邻居非常友好,经常互相帮忙。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de línjū fēicháng yǒuhǎo, jīngcháng hùxiāng bāngmáng.
example.english: Our neighbors are very friendly, and we often help each other out.
example.fact: 邻居 combines 邻 (“adjacent, nearby”) with 居 (“to reside, dwell”) — literally “one who dwells nearby.” English “neighbor” is built the same way, from Old English “nēah” (near) plus “gebūr” (dweller) — two unrelated languages independently landing on the identical logic.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū yǎngle yì zhī māo.
examples.english: My neighbor has a cat.

examples.pinyin: Línjūmen chángcháng yìqǐ liáotiān.
examples.english: The neighbors often chat together.

components.note: 今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 今年夏天特别热。
example.pinyin: Jīnnián xiàtiān tèbié rè.
example.english: This summer has been especially hot.
example.fact: 今年, 今天 (“today”), and 今晚 (“tonight”) all share the prefix 今 (“the present, now”) — once a learner spots this one recurring syllable, the whole family of “this ___” time words becomes predictable rather than needing separate memorization.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīnnián xiǎng qù xué yóuyǒng.
examples.english: This year I want to learn to swim.

examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de dōngtiān tèbié lěng.
examples.english: This winter is especially cold.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 我心里一直想着这件事。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xīnli yìzhí xiǎngzhe zhè jiàn shì.
example.english: I've been thinking about this the whole time, deep down.
example.fact: 心里 literally means “inside the heart” (心 “heart” + 里 “inside”) and is Mandarin's default way to talk about private, unspoken thoughts — 心里想 (“to think to oneself”) describes something felt internally, in contrast to 说 (“to say”), which brings a thought out into the open.

examples.pinyin: Tā xīnli hěn nánguò.
examples.english: He feels very sad inside.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīnli yǒu huà xiǎng duì nǐ shuō.
examples.english: I have something in my heart I want to tell you.

components.note: 尸 (body/roof) — the top-left cover, as in 层 and 局. In 展 it works like a cover over cloth that is spread out; memory aid, shape is partly simplified.
衣 (clothing) — a bit of this sits inside 展. Dictionary story: laying out clothes to display them, hence 'unfold, exhibit' in 展示.
示 (show) — an altar, a table for offerings; as the radical 礻 it marks rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福, 社, 祝.

example.hanzi: 这家博物馆展示了很多古代文物。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā bówùguǎn zhǎnshì le hěn duō gǔdài wénwù.
example.english: This museum displays many ancient artifacts.
example.fact: 展示 leans formal — exhibitions, presentations, formal demonstrations — while casual speech more often just says 给...看 (“show to...”); the newer slangy 秀 (a phonetic loanword from English “show,” as in 脱口秀, “talk show”) covers similar ground with a much more casual flavor.

examples.hanzi: 她向大家展示了新买的手机。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng dàjiā zhǎnshìle xīn mǎi de shǒujī.
examples.english: She showed everyone her newly bought phone.

examples.hanzi: 这次展览展示了很多年轻人的作品。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì zhǎnlǎn zhǎnshìle hěn duō niánqīngrén de zuòpǐn.
examples.english: This exhibition displays many works by young people.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 这首歌的调子很好听。
example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de diàozi hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: The tune of this song is very pleasant.
example.fact: 调 has two readings: diào (tune, tone, transfer, investigate: 声调, 调查, 调动) and tiáo (adjust, mix: 调整, 空调, 调皮). 空调 (air conditioner) is read kōngtiáo, so check the reading in each word.

examples.hanzi: 请把空调调到二十六度。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ kōngtiáo tiáo dào èrshíliù dù.
examples.english: Please set the air conditioner to 26 degrees.

examples.hanzi: 他的口音带着南方的腔调。
examples.pinyin: Tā de kǒuyīn dài zhe nánfāng de qiāngdiào.
examples.english: His accent has a southern lilt.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 他们打算下个月去意大利旅游。
example.pinyin: Tāmen dǎsuàn xià gè yuè qù Yìdàlì lǚyóu.
example.english: They're planning to travel to Italy next month.
example.fact: 意大利 is a phonetic transliteration of “Italia” — the three characters were picked mainly to approximate the sound (Yì-dà-lì), not for their literal meanings, the same strategy behind most Mandarin names for countries outside the historical Sinosphere, like 加拿大 (Jiānádà) for “Canada.”

examples.pinyin: Yìdàlì de bǐsà hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: Italian pizza is very famous.

examples.hanzi: 我对意大利的历史很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì Yìdàlì de lìshǐ hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I'm very interested in the history of Italy.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and language, as in 说 say, 请 please, 谢 thank.
斥 (chì) is only a loose sound hint for sù.

example.hanzi: 他决定起诉那家公司。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng qǐsù nà jiā gōngsī.
example.english: He decided to sue that company.
example.fact: 起诉 is a formal legal term reserved for actually filing a lawsuit or bringing criminal charges — an everyday grievance instead reaches for much softer words like 抱怨 (“to complain”) or 投诉 (“to file a complaint,” e.g. to customer service), so hearing 起诉 signals the matter has escalated to court.

examples.pinyin: Tā yào qǐsù nà jiā gōngsī.
examples.english: She is going to sue that company.

examples.pinyin: Lǜshī jiànyì tā qǐsù duìfāng.
examples.english: The lawyer advised him to sue the other side.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他是个乐于助人的好人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì gè lèyú zhùrén de hǎorén.
example.english: He's a good person who loves helping others.
example.fact: 好人 is about as literal a compound as Mandarin offers — 好 (“good”) plus 人 (“person”) — but its very plainness is why it needs careful handling: in modern slang, calling someone a 好人 can faintly imply “nice, but a pushover” (as in 好人卡, the “good-person card” of being turned down romantically), so tone and context matter more than the dictionary gloss suggests.

examples.hanzi: 他是个好人，大家都喜欢他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge hǎorén, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: He is a good person and everyone likes him.

examples.pinyin: Hǎorén yǒu hǎobào.
examples.english: Good people are rewarded.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
王 (king) — three bars for heaven, people and earth joined by a vertical: the ruler who links them. As 玉 jade with its dot dropped it also marks jewels: 球, 玩.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的国王非常受人民爱戴。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de guówáng fēicháng shòu rénmín àidài.
example.english: This country's king is deeply loved by his people.
example.fact: 王 by itself already meant “king, monarch” (it's also the common surname Wáng, originally a title before it became a family name) — 国王 clarifies the specifically national, ruling sense by prefixing 国 (“country, state”), setting it apart from other extended uses of 王 like 龙王, the mythological “Dragon King.”

examples.hanzi: 国王住在一座古老的城堡里。
examples.pinyin: Guówáng zhù zài yí zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo lǐ.
examples.english: The king lives in an ancient castle.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的国王很爱他的人民。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de guówáng hěn ài tā de rénmín.
examples.english: The king in the story loves his people very much.

components.note: 可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).

example.hanzi: 我哥哥在北京工作。
example.pinyin: Wǒ gēge zài Běijīng gōngzuò.
example.english: My older brother works in Beijing.
example.fact: 哥 on its own is mostly a term of address ("Big Brother"), while the family term is the doubled 哥哥. Friendly speech stretches it: 大哥 for any respected older man, and 哥们儿 for a buddy, especially in northern speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.english: My older brother is three years older than me.

examples.hanzi: 那位歌手是大哥的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi gēshǒu shì dàgē de péngyou.
examples.english: That singer is my eldest brother's friend.

components.note: 长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 我在北京长大,但现在住在上海。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài Běijīng zhǎngdà, dàn xiànzài zhù zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: I grew up in Beijing, but now I live in Shanghai.
example.fact: 长 is a genuine two-way character: read cháng it means “long” (长城, “the Great Wall”), and read zhǎng it means “to grow, to be senior” (长大, 家长 “parent”) — one character splitting into two unrelated pronunciations and meaning-families, with no visual cue to tell them apart.

examples.hanzi: 等你长大了，就会明白的。
examples.pinyin: Děng nǐ zhǎngdà le, jiù huì míngbai de.
examples.english: When you grow up, you'll understand.

examples.pinyin: Háizi zhǎngdà de zhēn kuài.
examples.english: Children grow up so fast.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — the top. Memory aid: grains of rice sorted by size 大 — sorted into groups, a kind (人类). Not proven etymology.
類 (traditional) — used for 'kind, class' with 犬 and 页. 类 is the simplified shape and keeps only a fragment of it.

example.hanzi: 你喜欢哪一类电影？
example.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan nǎ yí lèi diànyǐng?
example.english: What kind of movies do you like?
example.fact: 类 groups things into broad categories and works like a measure word in 这类人 or 一类问题. Compare 种 (zhǒng), which stresses a specific variety; 类 sits a level above it, as in 分类 (to classify) and 种类 (kinds).

examples.hanzi: 书店里的书分成很多类。
examples.pinyin: Shūdiàn lǐ de shū fēnchéng hěn duō lèi.
examples.english: The books in the bookstore are divided into many categories.

examples.pinyin: Zhè lèi wèntí hěn chángjiàn.
examples.english: This kind of problem is very common.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.

example.hanzi: 我把钱交给了银行职员。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ qián jiāo gěi le yínháng zhíyuán.
example.english: I handed the money over to the bank clerk.
example.fact: 交给 commonly appears inside a 把-construction (把 + object + 交给 + recipient), fronting the thing being handed over before the verb — a pattern worth noticing for verbs describing a literal physical transfer, where 把 often reads more naturally than plain subject-verb-object order.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fēng xìn jiāogěi tā.
examples.english: Please hand this letter to him.

examples.hanzi: 老师把作业交给了学生。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ zuòyè jiāogěile xuésheng.
examples.english: The teacher handed the homework to the students.

components.note: 王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — precious jade, an omen of luck; also in 球 ball, 珠 pearl.
耑 (duān) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 端 duān.

example.hanzi: 瑞雪兆丰年。
example.pinyin: Ruì xuě zhào fēngnián.
example.english: A timely snow foretells a good harvest year.
example.fact: 瑞 is almost always bound inside words and sayings. 瑞雪 (timely snow) is a winter blessing for farmers because snow cover protects wheat, which is why the proverb ties it to a bumper year. It also appears in country names like 瑞士 (Switzerland) and 瑞典 (Sweden).

examples.pinyin: Tā shì Ruìdiǎn rén.
examples.english: He is Swedish.

examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de ruìxuě lái de hěn zǎo.
examples.english: This year's auspicious snow came very early.

components.note: 尸 (body, a crouching figure) — also in 屁 and 屎; 尿 is body plus 水 (water).
水 (water) — liquid passed from the body.

example.hanzi: 宝宝尿床了。
example.pinyin: Bǎobao niào chuáng le.
example.english: The baby wet the bed.
example.fact: 尿 is both noun and verb: 尿尿 is the childlike word, 撒尿 is blunt, and 小便 is the polite register. Its measure word is 泡 (pāo), as in 一泡尿. In some northern speech the noun is read suī instead of niào.

examples.pinyin: Háizi wǎnshang niào le yí cì chuáng.
examples.english: The child wet the bed once at night.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù cèsuǒ niàoniào.
examples.english: I want to go to the toilet to pee.

components.note: 尸 (body) — marks the body and its functions, as in 尿 urine, 屁 fart; 屎 is bodily waste, with 米 for what is eaten.

example.hanzi: 小狗在院子里拉屎了。
example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu zài yuànzi lǐ lā shǐ le.
example.english: The puppy pooped in the yard.
example.fact: 屎 is crude, and the verb phrase is 拉屎 (literally "pull poop"); polite speech uses 大便. The character also shows up in harmless compounds like 眼屎 (eye gunk) and 耳屎 (earwax).

examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái de shǐ hěn chòu.
examples.english: The baby's poop is smelly.

examples.pinyin: Bié cǎi dào gǒushǐ.
examples.english: Don't step in dog poop.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 陪 is to sit by one's side.
咅 (pōu) is a loose sound clue; same part in 培 péi, 赔 péi, 倍 bèi.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; 审 is a hearing held in a hall.
申 (shēn) is a near sound match for shěn; also in 神 shén, 伸 shēn.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.

example.hanzi: 陪审团经过三天讨论后做出了判决。
example.pinyin: Péishěntuán jīngguò sān tiān tǎolùn hòu zuòchū le pànjué.
example.english: After three days of deliberation, the jury reached a verdict.
example.fact: 陪审团 is a modern legal loan-translation coined for a Western institution — 陪审 (“to accompany in judging,” i.e., to serve as a juror) plus 团 (“group”). Mainland Chinese courts don't actually use jury trials, relying instead on a system of lay assessors, so the word shows up far more in translated foreign news and legal dramas than in domestic reporting.

examples.hanzi: 陪审团需要一致同意才能决定。
examples.pinyin: Péishěntuán xūyào yízhì tóngyì cáinéng juédìng.
examples.english: The jury needs unanimous agreement to decide.

examples.hanzi: 陪审团成员有十二个人。
examples.pinyin: Péishěntuán chéngyuán yǒu shí'èr ge rén.
examples.english: The jury has twelve members.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 项 first meant the neck.
工 (gōng) is only a loose sound hint for xiàng.
目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.

example.hanzi: 这个项目预计需要六个月才能完成。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù yùjì xūyào liù gè yuè cáinéng wánchéng.
example.english: This project is expected to take six months to complete.
example.fact: 项目 covers a surprising range of English words depending on context — “project” in business, “item” on a list or budget, “event” in sports (田径项目, “track and field event”) — one Mandarin compound doing the job of three fairly distinct English nouns.

examples.hanzi: 这个项目需要很多人合作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiàngmù xūyào hěn duō rén hézuò.
examples.english: This project needs many people to cooperate.

examples.hanzi: 你们的项目进展得怎么样？
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen de xiàngmù jìnzhǎn de zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: How is your project going?

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 请大家集中注意力,认真听讲。
example.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā jízhōng zhùyìlì, rènzhēn tīngjiǎng.
example.english: Everyone please focus your attention and listen carefully.
example.fact: 集中 works as both a verb (“to concentrate, gather together”) and a stative description (“concentrated, centralized”) without changing form — covering both a physical gathering of things (人口集中, “the population is concentrated”) and a mental focusing of attention (集中注意力), two senses English usually keeps apart with different words.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ jízhōng jīnglì zuò zuòyè.
examples.english: Please focus your energy on your homework.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā jízhōng zài ménkǒu děng chē.
examples.english: Everyone gathers at the door to wait for the bus.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 说实话,我根本不喜欢这个计划。
example.pinyin: Shuō shíhuà, wǒ gēnběn bù xǐhuan zhège jìhuà.
example.english: To tell the truth, I don't like this plan at all.
example.fact: 实话 shows up almost exclusively inside the fixed opener “说实话” (“to speak honestly,” “to tell the truth”) — a discourse marker that, much like English “honestly” or “to be frank,” signals the speaker is about to say something candid, and possibly blunt.

examples.hanzi: 你跟我说实话，到底怎么了？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gēn wǒ shuō shíhuà, dàodǐ zěnme le?
examples.english: Tell me the truth, what's wrong?

examples.hanzi: 实话告诉你，我也不知道。
examples.pinyin: Shíhuà gàosu nǐ, wǒ yě bù zhīdào.
examples.english: To tell you the truth, I don't know either.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 她听到这个消息后,脸上露出惊讶的表情。
example.pinyin: Tā tīngdào zhège xiāoxi hòu, liǎn shàng lùchū jīngyà de biǎoqíng.
example.english: After hearing the news, a look of surprise appeared on her face.
example.fact: 表情 combines 表 (“to show, express” — from an old image of a fur garment worn on the outside, hence “outer, surface”) with 情 (“feeling, emotion”) — literally “the outward showing of feeling,” a compositional logic that survives almost unchanged in the English loan-translation “facial expression.”

examples.pinyin: Tā de biǎoqíng hěn yánsù.
examples.english: His expression is very serious.

examples.pinyin: Bǎobao de biǎoqíng zhēn kě'ài.
examples.english: The baby's expression is really cute.

components.note: 目 (eye) — a cap pulled over the eyes: to cover, to push ahead blindly. Used in 冒险 and 感冒.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: a steep place, a risky pass.
佥 (qiān) is a loose sound clue for xiǎn; 佥 also in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 验 yàn.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢冒险,经常一个人去爬山。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan màoxiǎn, jīngcháng yí gè rén qù páshān.
example.english: He likes taking risks and often goes mountain climbing alone.
example.fact: 冒险 works as both a verb (“to take a risk”) and a noun (“an adventure”), letting one word cover ground English splits between “to risk” and “adventure” — 冒险家 (“adventurer”) and 冒险精神 (“adventurous spirit”) both build directly on the same root.

examples.hanzi: 爬山有点冒险，但是很有趣。
examples.pinyin: Páshān yǒudiǎn màoxiǎn, dànshì hěn yǒuqù.
examples.english: Mountain climbing is a bit risky but very fun.

examples.pinyin: Zuò shēngyi chángcháng yào màoxiǎn.
examples.english: Doing business often means taking risks.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 多喝水对身体有很多好处。
example.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ duì shēntǐ yǒu hěn duō hǎochu.
example.english: Drinking more water has a lot of benefits for your health.
example.fact: The exact same two characters, with the second syllable kept in its full third tone as hǎochǔ, form a separate and much rarer word meaning “easy to get along with” — a tone-only homograph just like 告诉's rare legal-register reading elsewhere in this deck. The everyday, high-frequency word is this neutral-toned hǎochu, “benefit, advantage” — the sense used here.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò duì nǐ méiyǒu hǎochu.
examples.english: Doing this brings you no benefit.

examples.hanzi: 他从这件事中得到了不少好处。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng zhè jiàn shì zhōng dédàole bùshǎo hǎochu.
examples.english: He got quite a few benefits from this matter.

components.note: 木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 请在表格里写你的名字。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài biǎogé lǐ xiě nǐ de míngzi.
example.english: Please write your name in the table.
example.fact: 格 is mostly a building block of compounds: 表格 (form), 价格 (price), 性格 (personality), 资格 (qualification). The idea behind them all is a fixed frame that something must fit into. It also names the boxes of a grid: 一格 is one square or one bar of signal.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de jiàgé bú guì.
examples.english: The price of this clothing is not high.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè hěn yǒu fēnggé de rén.
examples.english: He is a person with a lot of style.

components.note: 工 (work) — a left hand 𠂇 with 工 (work): the hand that helps with work; compare 右 on the right.

example.hanzi: 请往左拐。
example.pinyin: Qǐng wǎng zuǒ guǎi.
example.english: Please turn left.
example.fact: 左右 is both the pair "left and right" and, after a number, "approximately": 三十岁左右 means around thirty. In politics 左 maps onto "the Left" as in English, but in much ancient usage 右 was the side of honour.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiàng yòu guǎi, ránhòu xiàng zuǒ zǒu.
examples.english: Turn right, and then go left.

examples.pinyin: Tā de zuǒshǒu shòushāng le.
examples.english: His left hand is injured.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.

example.hanzi: 我们周末去海边玩。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù hǎibiān wán.
example.english: We are going to the seaside this weekend.
example.fact: 海 stretches into figurative "vast sea of" phrases: 人海 (sea of people), 云海 (sea of clouds). The city 上海 literally means "on the sea". Large inland lakes can also be called 海, such as 中南海 in Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Dàhǎi hěn lán, yě hěn dà.
examples.english: The sea is blue and vast.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Hǎinán lǚyóu.
examples.english: I want to travel to Hainan.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.
皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.
鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了一个吸血鬼的爱情故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshù le yí gè xīxuèguǐ de àiqíng gùshi.
example.english: This movie tells the love story of a vampire.
example.fact: 吸血鬼 is a literal, descriptive loan-translation rather than a phonetic borrowing of “vampire” — 吸血 (“to suck blood”) plus 鬼 (“ghost, spirit”). Unlike 意大利 (a purely sound-based transliteration also in this batch), this word was built entirely from existing Chinese roots to describe what a vampire does.

examples.hanzi: 万圣节的时候，孩子们打扮成吸血鬼。
examples.pinyin: Wànshèngjié de shíhou, háizimen dǎbàn chéng xīxuèguǐ.
examples.english: At Halloween, the kids dress up as vampires.

examples.hanzi: 我觉得吸血鬼的故事很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde xīxuèguǐ de gùshi hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: I think vampire stories are interesting.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; here part of the simplified form 胜 for victory.
生 (shēng) is a near sound match for shèng; also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 我们的球队终于赢得了这场比赛的胜利。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de qiúduì zhōngyú yíngdé le zhè chǎng bǐsài de shènglì.
example.english: Our team finally achieved victory in this match.
example.fact: 胜利 doubles up two characters that each already point toward triumph on their own: 胜 (“to overcome, defeat,” as in 胜出 “to win out”) and 利 (“gain, advantage,” as in 利益 “benefit”) — pairing two near-synonyms into one intensified word, a common Mandarin strategy for building two-character verbs and nouns.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú qǔdéle shènglì!
examples.english: We finally achieved victory!

examples.hanzi: 胜利属于坚持到最后的人。
examples.pinyin: Shènglì shǔyú jiānchí dào zuìhòu de rén.
examples.english: Victory belongs to those who persevere to the end.

meanings: to go as far as to

components.note: 音 (sound) — a piece of music 音 played to its end by a person 儿: finishing, then "at last" or unexpectedly.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 他竟然一个人爬上了那座山。
example.pinyin: Tā jìngrán yí gè rén pá shàng le nà zuò shān.
example.english: To my surprise, he climbed that mountain all by himself.
example.fact: 竟然 is an adverb of attitude rather than fact — it adds no new information to a sentence, only the speaker's surprise at it. Removing 竟然 leaves a sentence's literal meaning untouched while stripping out all the astonishment.

examples.pinyin: Tā jìngrán wàngle wǒ de míngzi.
examples.english: He actually forgot my name.

examples.hanzi: 这么简单的题，你竟然做错了。
examples.pinyin: Zhème jiǎndān de tí, nǐ jìngrán zuòcuò le.
examples.english: You actually got such an easy question wrong.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sunlight falling on everything: universal, common. 普 also sounds out 谱 pǔ.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 他只是一个普通的上班族,过着简单的生活。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǐshì yí gè pǔtōng de shàngbānzú, guòzhe jiǎndān de shēnghuó.
example.english: He's just an ordinary office worker, living a simple life.
example.fact: 普通 is the root behind 普通话 (“Putonghua,” literally “the common speech”), the official Mainland term for Standard Mandarin — the same “common, general” sense behind the everyday adjective also names the entire standardized national language.

examples.hanzi: 这是一件很普通的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí jiàn hěn pǔtōng de yīfu.
examples.english: This is a very ordinary piece of clothing.

examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de shì pǔtōnghuà.
examples.english: He speaks Mandarin.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 他想当官。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng dāng guān.
example.english: He wants to become an official.
example.fact: 当官 (to become an official) has a hint of ambition and sometimes irony. The same character gives 器官 (organ) and 五官 (the five facial features) because those are the body's "officers", each with a duty. 官方 means "official" in the sense of authorized.

examples.pinyin: Tā dāngshàngle dà guān.
examples.english: He became a high official.

examples.hanzi: 他是一名警官，每天在街上巡逻。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng jǐngguān, měitiān zài jiē shang xúnluó.
examples.english: He is a police officer who patrols the streets every day.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 这条路一直往前走。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù yìzhí wǎng qián zǒu.
example.english: Go straight ahead along this road.
example.fact: In 一直 the word means either "straight on" in space (一直走) or "all along, continuously" in time (他一直在等你). 直 also carries "frank": 直说 is to speak bluntly, and 直接 means direct.

examples.hanzi: 这根线不直，请再拉直一点。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gēn xiàn bù zhí, qǐng zài lāzhí yìdiǎn.
examples.english: This line isn't straight; please pull it a bit straighter.

examples.hanzi: 他说话很直，从不拐弯抹角。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà hěn zhí, cóng bù guǎiwān-mòjiǎo.
examples.english: He speaks very directly and never beats around the bush.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
示 (show) — an altar, a table for offerings; as the radical 礻 it marks rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福, 社, 祝.

example.hanzi: 他点了点头,表示同意。
example.pinyin: Tā diǎnle diǎn tóu, biǎoshì tóngyì.
example.english: He nodded his head, indicating his agreement.
example.fact: 表示 overlaps heavily with 表现 (“to show, display”) and 表达 (“to express,” usually feelings or ideas in words) — all three share the root 表 (“to show”) but attach different second characters to specialize: 示 for signaling, 现 for outward manifestation, 达 for conveying through language.

examples.hanzi: 他表示很感谢大家的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Tā biǎoshì hěn gǎnxiè dàjiā de bāngzhù.
examples.english: He expressed that he was very grateful for everyone's help.

examples.hanzi: 这个红灯表示不能过马路。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge hóngdēng biǎoshì bù néng guò mǎlù.
examples.english: This red light means you can't cross the road.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a hand 爪 pressing on a person 卩: to stamp or press a mark, hence seal and print.
象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.hanzi: 他给我留下了很好的印象。
example.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ liúxià le hěn hǎo de yìnxiàng.
example.english: He left a very good impression on me.
example.fact: 印象 combines 印 (“to stamp, print” — originally a hand pressing down a seal) with 象 (“image, shape,” from a pictograph of an elephant later broadened to mean any visual form) — together, “an image stamped [in the mind],” a metaphor strikingly close to English “impression,” from Latin “imprimere,” to press into.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市给我的印象很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge chéngshì gěi wǒ de yìnxiàng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This city made a very good impression on me.

examples.hanzi: 我对那件事没有印象了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì nà jiàn shì méiyǒu yìnxiàng le.
examples.english: I no longer remember that matter.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 她出生在一个小村庄。
example.pinyin: Tā chūshēng zài yí gè xiǎo cūnzhuāng.
example.english: She was born in a small village.
example.fact: 出生 is a resultative compound built from 出 (“to come out, exit”) and 生 (“to be born, to live”) — literally “to come out into life.” Grammatically it's a full verb, not an adjective, so English “born” (as in “I was born in 1990”) maps onto a verb phrase in Mandarin rather than a passive participle.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chūshēng zài yí ge xiǎo chéngshì.
examples.english: I was born in a small city.

examples.hanzi: 你是在哪个城市出生的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì zài nǎge chéngshì chūshēng de?
examples.english: Which city were you born in?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
尸 (body/roof) — the top-left cover, as in 层 and 局. In 展 it works like a cover over cloth that is spread out; memory aid, shape is partly simplified.
衣 (clothing) — a bit of this sits inside 展. Dictionary story: laying out clothes to display them, hence 'unfold, exhibit' in 展示.

example.hanzi: 这项研究最近有了新的进展。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng yánjiū zuìjìn yǒule xīn de jìnzhǎn.
example.english: This research has recently made new progress.
example.fact: 进展 functions as both a noun (“progress,” as in 有进展, “there's progress”) and a verb (“to progress, make headway”) without changing form — one word doing double duty where English needs “progress” and “to progress” as two separate parts of speech.

examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò jìnzhǎn de hěn shùnlì.
examples.english: The work is progressing smoothly.

examples.hanzi: 这个项目没有什么进展。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiàngmù méiyǒu shénme jìnzhǎn.
examples.english: There has been no progress on this project.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 估 is a trader's guess at value.
古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue; same part in 姑 gū, 枯 kū, 苦 kǔ.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.

example.hanzi: 我估计这次旅行大概需要花费一万块钱。
example.pinyin: Wǒ gūjì zhè cì lǚxíng dàgài xūyào huāfèi yí wàn kuài qián.
example.english: I estimate this trip will cost around ten thousand yuan.
example.fact: In casual speech, 估计 has drifted from its literal sense “to calculate, estimate” into a hedging word much like English “I bet” or “I reckon” — saying 我估计他不会来了 (“I bet he's not coming”) doesn't require any actual arithmetic, just an informed hunch.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gūjì tā xiàwǔ cái huì lái.
examples.english: I estimate he won't come until the afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 请你估计一下需要多少时间。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ gūjì yíxià xūyào duōshao shíjiān.
examples.english: Please estimate how much time is needed.

components.note: 乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".

example.hanzi: 祝你生日快乐！
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè!
example.english: Happy birthday to you!
example.fact: 乐 is a classic two-reading character: lè means "happy" (快乐), but yuè means "music" (音乐). The meanings are connected, since music was the original source of joy. As a surname it is Yuè.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèyì bāng nǐ de máng.
examples.english: I'm very happy to help you.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢音乐，觉得学琴是一件乐事。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yīnyuè, juéde xué qín shì yí jiàn lèshì.
examples.english: He likes music and finds learning the piano a joy.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 请把会议的时间和地点发给大家。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ huìyì de shíjiān hé dìdiǎn fā gěi dàjiā.
example.english: Please send everyone the time and location of the meeting.
example.fact: 地点 combines 地 (“ground, earth”) with 点 (“point, dot”) — literally “a point on the ground.” English arrives at a near-identical image from a different direction: “location” traces back to Latin “locus,” “place,” narrowed down to a specific spot.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dìdiǎn lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.english: This place is very close to the school.

examples.hanzi: 你们约在什么地点见面？
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen yuē zài shénme dìdiǎn jiànmiàn?
examples.english: At what place did you arrange to meet?
